findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with white debris. The PIC was informed and believed the build-up to be due to hard water. The ice machine was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. Ensure staff are monitoring the cleanliness of the machine and sanitizing often to prevent accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw shell eggs stored on the top shelf of the two-door cooler above lettuce and other produce items. PIC was informed of proper storage order and eggs were moved to the bottom shelf. Ensure raw food items such as eggs or chicken are stored below ready-to-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed dish machine to measure 0ppm chlorine during today’s inspection. PIC was informed and discovered that the sanitizer was replaced with a bottle of detergent instead of a new bottle of sanitizer. PIC left facility and purchased new sanitizer from GFS. The new sanitizer was installed and primed through the machine. The dish machine then measured 100ppm chlorine. Ensure staff are monitoring sanitizer concentration in the dish machine using the available test strips.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed boxes of ranch dressing, napkins, and cups to be stored on the floor of the dry storage area. PIC was informed of proper storage conditions for food or food-contact items. Extra blue crates will be used to elevate items off the floor, as space is limited in the dry storage area.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed kitchen dish machine to not be dispensing chlorine sanitizer in rinse cycle. Service machine to ensure chlorine sanitizer is dispensed in rinse cycle.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed boxes of single service cups and napkins to be stored on the floor in the storage area. Store single service items at least 6 inches above ground. 

Maintain boxes of single use items at least six inches above the floor. 4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed interior of prep cooler and upright coolers in kitchen to be soiled with food splash and debris. Clean and sanitize interior of kitchen coolers. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed wash solution in kitchen dish machine to not be reaching 120F. Dish machine was run for 5 cycles. Max temperature registered for each cycle was: 95F, 105F, 108F, 112F, and 116F. Service dish machine to raise wash solution temp to 120F. 

4-501.110: (A) Temperature of the wash solution in spray type warewashers using hot water may not be less than: 165F for stationary rack-single temperature, 150F for stationary rack-dual temperature machine, 160F single tank, conveyor-dual temperature, 150F multitank conveyor-multitemperature. (B) Temperature for wash solution using chemical SANITIZER may not be less than 120F.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed the inside of the ice machine to be soiled with debris. Properly clean and sanitize the inside of the ice machine to protect food. Ice was removed from machine and the drop guard was cleaned and properly sanitized. 4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Observed the items in the cold holding to be missing dates. Also the milk that is open in the door of the cold holding unit does not have an opened date on it. Dates were added to the packaged items to ensure that they will be sold or discarded in 7 days. 3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Observed the ceiling above where the sandwich maker stands to be soiled with dust. Also, the top shelf of the wire shelving unit holding bread in bags is soiled with accumulated dust. Clean these areas and maintain them clean. 6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. 

The dish machine would not register sanitizer on the inspector's test strips. PIC is unsure how to provide maintenance on the machine and will be calling ECO Lab for maintenance.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Two different chemical sanitizers are observed used in the facility. Neither sanitizer has test strips available during the inspection. PIC is instructed to maintain test strips for all sanitizers used in the food areas and on food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

The inside of the upright cooler next to the sandwich prep area is observed visibly soiled on the inside surfaces. PIC is instructed to clean and then clean often enough to prevent soil accumulation.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11  (C) Employee observed drinking from an uncovered cup in the food preparation area. Provide a lid and straw for beverage cups. Reference 2-401.11. Employee was directed to put lid on cup.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizing rinse at dish machine measured at 0 ppm chlorine concentration. A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114. Ecolab arrived during inspection and repaired machine. Machine is now testing at 100ppm Cl.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15  (C) The method of cooling bean salsa is inadequate. Food must be uncovered during cooling, if protected from overhead contamination. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15. Also, place date and time on cooling items. Any itme placed into the cold holding to cool shall have date and time.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed cookie bars to be wrapped for sale with no labeling. Properly label items like this according to the directions below. 750-110g Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name;, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used.

Chicken salad observed in the front cooler does not have time label but is cooling. Add time labels to all items that are placed into a cooler to cool. (aka with a temperature above 41F)  750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed some wood containers in the facility. Remove wooden storage containers. 750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Glass front cooler holding Redi Whip and stainless cooler in front do not have appropriate thermometers. Provide appropriate thermometers for all cooling units. 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Two bags of flour are observed to be stored on the floor in the cafe. Store food properly. 750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.
Observed a cup of coffee to be sitting on a shelf holding other food items. Cup was removed to dish area. 750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: The water cup/drain area on the side of the dish machine has heavy soil accumulation. The handles are also greasy. Clean and maintain clean. 750-830i All dish washing machines shall be thoroughly cleaned at least once a day or more often when necessary to maintain them in satisfactory operating condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Fronts of the cooler and freezer in back are heavily soiled. Areas around the cafe equipment including the tracks on the glass display cooler are soiled. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: A box of pie boxes is observed to be on the floor in the back. Store the  single use items properly. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - (R) Chlorine and quat test kits were not available for checking sanitizer concentrations. Chlorine strips are needed for the dish machine, and quat strips are needed for the wall mounted sanitizer and Redi San spray bottles.  Manger stated Ecolab was just out to check everything and was supposed to be bringing more test strips.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - (R) The spout of the coffee machine above the grounds basket was soiled with heavy buildup. Clean the spout above the grounds basket daily/as needed to eliminate buildup.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. In-use equipment and utensils (i.e. knives, cutting boards, etc.) need to be cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - A) Coffee filters were observed in wire basket uncovered. Provide a cover for the top of the basket.

B) Container by coffee maker used for plastic fork storage had dried syrup splash inside. Clean the container as needed, and consider storing in an area away from syrup bottle.

C) Boxes containing hinged lid containers, plastic lids, and insulted cups were observed on the floor in dry storage area. Delivery was last received on Friday. Provide means to elevate the boxes up off the floor at least 6 inches until items can be put away by students in proper storage area.

Single service articles shall be stored, handles, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from contamination.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floor beneath Pepsi reach-in cooler by the drive thru window was soiled with general buildup. Clean the floor in the aforementioned area.

Floors shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Manager did not wash hands between tasks - went from helping at cash register to putting on gloves to help with food prep. Manager discarded gloves, properly washed hands, and put on a new pair of gloves before continuing with food prep.
Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment. Hands must always be washed between handling money and prior to doing any other tasks related  to food handling, including handling clean equipment and single service articles (i.e. coffee filters, etc.). Hands are to be washed prior to putting on gloves and between glove changes.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Wet wiping cloth for stem thermometer was damp with water in a tupperware container, but manager noted sanitizer had not yet been added to the container. Manager stated no foods were prepared yet that required a temperature check with the stem thermometer. Manager was advised on proper storage of wet wiping cloths in a sanitizer solution at all times. Do not set out a wiping cloth that is damp with water only just in case it would be mistaken for one that is in sanitizer/ready for use. Container was removed from the prep area, and the wiping cloth was placed in soiled linen storage container.
Moist cloths used for wiping food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text:
750.1170 - Drive thru window was open upon arrival of inspector. A screen is not present at the drive thru window.  Management was advised the window can not be left open between uses. The drive thru window was closed. A tight fitting, vermin proof screen needs to be installed at the drive thru window if staff want to be able to keep the window open.
Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.
